cells.tense: You are here with the pen, and thought is doing what it was built for.
cells.act: start something for the spark of starting
cells.ask: Pick something you want and start it without first working out whether it will succeed. Just the first move.
cells.core:
In what you want, the strategies are working — you can see through to the logic of a thing and keep moving toward what you chose. It looks like quick reading, quick cutting, quick direction. What holds it steady is quieter than the speed: the thinking has actually been tested, and it stays honest with the goal in view.

Start one thing for the simple charge of it — no plan for the finish, no test to pass. Choose something that pulls you, take the first step, and leave the rest unwritten for now. The spark is the point. What you want next gets clearer when you give one small beginning somewhere to land.

cells.tense: You are bracing against a future that cannot be fully written in.
cells.act: set a boundary and hold it
cells.ask: Name one line about your time or energy and keep it the next time it gets pushed.
cells.core:
Toward what you want, thought is running past the thing itself. Plans get made for a future that has not arrived, and the plans start acting like orders for other people to obey. The push is meant as direction — from inside it feels like getting somewhere — but the goal keeps moving out of reach, and the people you want to arrive with get left behind the plan.

Set one boundary and hold it, plainly. Pick a line about your time or energy and keep it the next time it gets pushed. A boundary held is a real thing you can point to; it gives the momentum something solid to turn toward instead of pushing further out.

cells.tense: You are still standing at a door that is already behind you.
cells.act: pursue the emotional truth with someone
cells.ask: Ask someone close what this season has felt like for them, and stay with their answer.
cells.core:
Where you are headed, the great machinery of strategy has gone quiet. The thinking that used to cut ahead now sits pointed at an older decision, running old sums. What you want most seems distant, and from here it can look like the direction itself has gone missing, though the goal may only be waiting for you to come back inside the present.

Ask someone close what this season has felt like for them, and stay in their answer without steering it anywhere. In hearing them, the part of you that pursues meaning gets its warmth back, and a step that had gone cold turns warm enough to take.
cells.sheetLine: A decision already made still has your attention.

cells.tense: The pen is down in a room you are already writing.
cells.act: hold space for what someone feels without fixing it
cells.ask: Let a feeling that is not yours sit with you for two minutes, and fix nothing.
cells.core:
The strategies are already moving — you are the one doing the fast thinking, setting the direction, having the answers — and by your own account you are not doing anything special at all. The hours get committed, the plans get made, and it registers as staying on top of things. The people at the table can see the steering hand; the hand itself has stopped taking credit for the wheel.

Hold space for what someone feels today without fixing it. Sit with a feeling that is not yours for two minutes, no solution attached. You will recognize the person doing that — and the strategy that follows will know where it came from.
